situation_en: Write a profile of a club, a school or a community group you know: what it does, who belongs to it and what makes it special. Choose only the most important facts.
Write both sides of a short text chat between you and a person you just met at an event (invent the person): open the conversation, keep it going with two questions and close it politely.
Write a post about something that shapes who you are, such as a hobby, a sport or a favorite food: what it is and why it matters.
Describe an object that shows your personality, such as something from school, a sport or a hobby, and explain what it says about you.
Write a review of a movie, a play or a show you saw: what it is about, what you liked, what you did not like and who should see it.
Write both sides of a text chat with a friend who wants to choose an event: suggest two events, give a reason for each and agree on one.
Write an ad for a performance, real or imagined, such as dance, circus or music: what it is, when and where it is and why people should come.
Describe a performance you saw, or imagine one at school or in the street: where it was, what the performers did and how the audience reacted.
Write a cover letter for a summer volunteer program or an internship: say why you are interested, what experience you have (school, sports or community) and what you can offer.
Write a polite email to a teacher to ask for a recommendation letter: what it is for, when you need it and how you will make the teacher’s job easier.
Write a résumé for a scholarship or a course: education, activities, skills and one achievement.
Write a short article about an opportunity that young people should know about, such as a course, a program or a competition: what it is, who can join and why it is good.
Write a post about an unforgettable experience near water, such as a beach, a river or a pool: where you were, what happened and why you will remember it. Use at least three vivid adjectives.
Write a story that begins with “Nobody expected what happened next.” Say what happened and how it ended.
Write an email inviting a friend to a river or beach day: the plan, what to bring and what you will do.
Describe an underwater scene that you imagine: what you can see and hear (for example, the waves above you), and how it makes you feel.
Write a formal email to your school cafeteria about healthier options: what you suggest and what the consequences could be if nothing changes.
Write a poster for a healthy-food day at school: what will happen, the time, the place and why it is useful.
Write a short report about snack choices in your class. Imagine you asked 20 classmates and invent the results: the question, the results and what they suggest.
Write a post about a habit that gives you energy or that you enjoy: what you do, how often and what changed.
Write a news story about a mysterious event in a town: what happened, who saw it, what experts say and what is still unknown.
Write the opening of a mystery story, about five sentences: where it happens, what the character sees and what the character does next. Use at least three -ly adverbs.
Invent a friend’s surprising news and write it as one message. Then write your replies: react, ask two questions and say what you think.
Write a short blog post about a mystery you would like to solve and why it interests you.
Describe a place where you like to spend time: where it is, what it looks like and why you like it. Organize your ideas in a clear order.
Write messages in a group chat about a shared space, such as a study room: say what you prefer and give two reasons.
Imagine a room for students to rent. Write an ad: the size, what is included and the price.
Write a short article about a problem in a neighborhood and one idea to improve it.
You are running late to meet a friend. You are going on a trip together. Send text messages: say what happened, when you will arrive and what your friend should do. Use an informal style.
Write a blog post about why travel matters to you: one place, one thing you learned and one wish. It can be a place you want to visit.
Write an email to a travel agency to solve a problem with your booking: what happened and what you need.
Write a post about returning to a place that you visited before, or imagine one: what changed and what stayed the same.
Write a product review: what you bought, what worked, what did not and whether you recommend it.
Write an ad to sell a used item: describe it, say the condition, the price and how to contact the seller.
Write a poster with five ways to reduce waste at school. Add a title and a short tip for each way.
Write messages to a friend to borrow or swap something: say what you want, offer something in return and agree on a day.
Write a personal email to a friend about a sports challenge you want to try, such as a race, a hike or a bike trip: what it is, why and how you will get ready.
Give advice to a friend who wants to improve at a sport: three tips and one mistake to avoid.
Write a profile of a person who pushed past their limits, such as a cave explorer or an athlete: what the person did, what the risks were and what we can learn.
Write a magazine interview with an explorer that you invent: three questions and the answers about a difficult trip.
Write a short article about how people communicate in different places: two examples about habits, not about whole countries, and one tip.
note: O gênero do livro nesta unidade é opinion essay, que fica no gerador 1. As situações abaixo são extras.

situation_en: Write an email to a friend in another country about a habit or a custom that surprised you: what it was and how you reacted.
Write a group chat: give your opinion about a school topic and reply politely to a classmate who disagrees.
Write a short story about two people from different countries who solve a problem by working together.

Write an article for a school website about a person you know or admire who is an expert, such as a chef or a firefighter: who the person is, what the person does and three things we can learn from this person.
Invent a group project. Write a message that apologizes for a mistake, and the reply that accepts the apology.
Write a story about a group that survives an unexpected problem, such as a storm or a lost path, and how the characters solve it.
Write a review of a book, a documentary or a podcast about survival or exploration, or invent one: what it is about and what you learned.
